facts.t: India borrowed duties from the USSR
facts.d: Fundamental Duties came in through the 42nd Amendment of 1976 on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation, modelled on the Soviet Constitution. Most liberal democracies — the United States, Australia, Canada, France — have no comparable chapter of citizen duties.

Article 51A originally listed ten duties. The 86th Amendment of 2002 added the eleventh — the duty of a parent or guardian to provide education to a child between six and fourteen — as the companion to the new Article 21A.

facts.t: Swaran Singh wanted duties with teeth
facts.d: The Committee recommended penalties for non-compliance, and duties to pay taxes and to vote. Parliament dropped all of that. What survived is a non-justiciable list — which is exactly why the Supreme Court is now hearing whether it can be made enforceable.

bank.q: Fundamental Duties were added on the recommendation of:
o: The Justice J. S. Verma Committee
bank.e: The Swaran Singh Committee, whose recommendations the 42nd Amendment implemented. The Verma Committee came much later, in 1999, and dealt with duty awareness rather than the duties themselves.

bank.q: With reference to Part IVA, consider the following statements:
s: They include a duty to pay taxes and to vote.
They are placed after the Directive Principles in the Constitution.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Duties to pay taxes and to vote were recommended by the Swaran Singh Committee but never included — a gap frequently cited as a limitation.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the criticisms of Fundamental Duties?
o: They are vaguely worded and hard to implement
They overlap with existing laws and policies
They are enforceable only against the State, not private citizens
Their placement after the DPSPs makes them appear less significant
bank.e: The problem is the opposite — they are not directly enforceable against anyone. Fundamental Duties address citizens, unlike Fundamental Rights, which chiefly bind the State.

bank.q: Match List I (case) with List II (its use of Fundamental Duties):
pairs: 1. Fundamental Rights must be read with DPSPs and Duties
B. M. C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath II (2000)
2. National awards connected to striving for excellence
C. Javed v. State of Haryana (2003)
3. Implementation of the Verma Committee recommendations directed
bank.e: Balaji Raghavan concerned national awards, Kamal Nath II environmental harm, Javed the integrated reading of rights and duties, and Ranganath Mishra directed action on the Verma Committee report.

bank.as: Courts prefer to translate Fundamental Duties into statute rather than enforce them directly.
bank.rs: Making duties directly punishable risks over-criminalisation and conflict with Fundamental Rights.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. The environmental duty under Article 51A(g) has effectively been given force through the Environment (Protection) Act regime, noise rules and firework time bands.

bank.q: Which case balanced the dignity of the national flag against freedom of expression, using duties to justify a proportionate restriction?
bank.e: Naveen Jindal (2004). Bijoe Emmanuel is the earlier national anthem case on the right to silence.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about the enforceability of Fundamental Duties:
s: The AIIMS Students' Union case held that duties guide but do not create directly enforceable obligations.
The Justice J. S. Verma Committee focused on curricula and public campaigns rather than criminal liability.
The Supreme Court has already declared Fundamental Duties legally enforceable.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The question of enforceability is being heard in Durga Dutt v. UoI; it has not been decided.

bank.q: All of the following have been proposed as additional Fundamental Duties EXCEPT:
o: A duty relating to family planning
A duty to serve in the armed forces
bank.e: Compulsory military service has never been part of this discussion in India. The other three, along with duties regarding science and technology, are the standard proposals.

bank.q: Article 51A(g), the environmental duty, is most often read alongside:
bank.e: Article 48A is the Directive Principle on protecting the environment; together with the Article 51A(g) duty they are read into Article 21 to generate an enforceable environmental right.

bank.q: Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
items: Justice J. S. Verma Committee reports
Fundamental Duties inserted into the Constitution
The eleventh duty on education is added
bank.e: Duties inserted by the 42nd Amendment (1976) → Balaji Raghavan (1995) → Verma Committee (1999) → the eleventh duty added by the 86th Amendment (2002).

bank.as: Fundamental Duties sit in Part IVA rather than in Part III.
bank.rs: The framers intended them to be morally binding rather than legally enforceable.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — though critics argue the placement after the Directive Principles makes them look like an afterthought rather than a deliberate design choice.
